s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal pain and distension with a large hepatic mass and vascular complications
salient_findings: Abdominal distension without guarding or rebound
Large mixed solid and cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe
IVC thrombus and near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
key_facts: 8-year-old girl with no significant medical history
1-week history of progressive abdominal pain
Nausea and vomiting
Abdominal distension without guarding or rebound
17 × 9 cm mixed solid and cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe
Compression of the inferior vena cava (IVC)
Percutaneous biopsy of the mass and placement of a drain
Persistent sanguineous output from the drain
Anemia and concern for hemorrhage
Infrarenal IVC thrombus and near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
Compression of the distal IVC at its junction with the right atrium

shortlist.label: Hepatoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large hepatic mass in a child with progressive abdominal pain and vascular complications

shortlist.label: Embryonal sarcoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive hepatic mass with compression of the inferior vena cava and risk of hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Hepatic angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatic mass with vascular invasion and risk of hemorrhage, although rare in children

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to embryonal sarcoma, with a large hepatic mass and vascular complications

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma with fibrolamellar variant
shortlist.why_kept: Although rare in children, the fibrolamellar variant can present with a large hepatic mass and vascular complications
